summary: Starts the backend and the frontend together for development and stops both on Ctrl+C.
purpose: Gives developers one command to run the whole app.
why: Likely reason: saves opening two terminals.
how: Starts the backend in the background from its virtual environment, waits five seconds, starts the frontend dev server in the background, prints the two web addresses, and waits. A Ctrl+C handler stops both processes.
inputs: The backend virtual environment and the frontend packages.
outputs: A running backend on port 8000 and frontend on port 3000.
risks: The fixed five-second wait is not a real readiness check, so the frontend may start before the backend is ready. If Ctrl+C is pressed before the handler is set, processes can keep running.
debug: If the backend does not respond, run its main program directly to see its error. If a port is busy, stop the other program using it.
